answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, so a single operator spinning up a nebula of fake accounts pays the bond once per identity. A prism of independent checks — reputation history, proof of useful work, and peer attestations — refracts that cost further, since each fake must also build a credible record. Like a willow that bends yet holds its roots, the economy stays open to honest newcomers while the price of forging many identities grows until it exceeds any gain from the attack.
